claim: The dependent reading of two languages requires at least three candidate languages.
evidence_summary: Suppose all students independently choose Welsh and German from five languages. That meets CGEL’s candidate-domain condition. If only those two are offered, assigning two to each student and assigning the same two to everyone have identical outcomes.
finding: Coincidence rebuts a requirement for distinct realized pairs, which CGEL does not impose here. Opening a third course could distinguish two policies. This leaves open whether the original sentence admits both readings in the two-language setting.
inference: Must at least two distinct pairs be available for two languages to take scope under each student?

evidence.passage: §8.3, p. 405, [12i] and the following paragraph. The condition is “three or more languages from which each student selects (or is assigned) a set of two”. Overlap among the resulting pairs is explicitly allowed.
